sentences.text: Gasosaurus was a carnivorous theropod characterized by strong legs and short arms.
This animal measured between 3.5 and 4 meters in length and weighed around 150 kilograms.

Scientists recognize the genus by features including amphiplatyan cervical and dorsal centra, low neural arches, plate-like neural spines, a humeral foramen, and expanded distal ends of the pubis and ischium.
Its limbs were built for power rather than speed, with short, strong legs and short arms.
The humerus of the holotype measures 237 millimeters in length.
The tibia is clearly shorter than the femur, measuring less than 370 millimeters compared to the femur's 425 millimeters, which is a primitive characteristic.
The name Gasosaurus combines the English word 'gasoline' with the Greek word for 'lizard'.
The species name 'constructus' honors the gasoline company that discovered the fossils at the Dashanpu quarry in Sichuan, China.
The name was assigned in honor of the oil company that found it at Dashanpu during a gas excavation in Sichuan Province, China, in the Lower Shaximiao Formation.
Paleontologists Dong Zhiming and Tang Zilu defined the fossils as the type species Gasosaurus constructus.
The first fossil is a postcranial skeleton with no known skull remains, cataloged as IVPP V7264.
Fossils of Gasosaurus were excavated near Dashanpu in Sichuan province, China.
Gasosaurus coexisted with other medium-sized theropods like Chuandongocoelurus and Kaijiangosaurus found in the Lower Shaximiao Formation.
It shared its environment with sauropods such as Datousaurus, Omeisaurus, and Protognathosaurus.
Smaller herbivorous dinosaurs like Xiaosaurus, Agilisaurus, and Huayangosaurus were present and served as prey.
Holtz (2000) classified Gasosaurus as a basal coelurosaurian, while later Holtz et al. (2004) suggested it might be a basal carnosaur or metriacanthosaurid.
Gasosaurus may represent the most basal known coelurosaurian or be close to the common ancestor of coelurosaurs and non-coelurosaurs, making it one of the oldest definitive tetanuran theropods.
Due to fragmentary fossils, Gasosaurus has an uncertain position within Tetanurae but is likely outside Coelurosauria.
In 2004, Holtz placed Gasosaurus within the broader group Avetheropoda.
The parent group of the genus Gasosaurus is Tetanurae.
Gasosaurus is classified under the class Reptilia.
Gasosaurus lived during the Middle Jurassic, between approximately 171.6 and 161.2 million years ago.
The time range for Gasosaurus is from the Bajocian to the Oxfordian, spanning 170.9 to 154.8 million years ago.
Some paleontologists speculate that Gasosaurus and Kaijiangosaurus might be the same species.
